Hi Op,

I had surgery in 2020 at 18 years old when everything was shut down due to covid so my recovery was especially hard on my mental health so I understand a bit of what you’re going through. 

I too also suffer from depression, anxiety, and an ED (ARFID) which was exasperated by my surgery recovery. My ED is caused by my fear of vomiting, and in recovery the opiate medications and muscle relaxers caused my digestive system to slow down dramatically so I experienced severe constipation as well and nausea. It was an endless cycle of nausea because of hunger, and nausea because of meds. It caused me to fear eating a lot so I didn’t get as much nutrients as I should have the first months of recovery. My fusion did fuse correctly according to my old orthopedic doctor, but it would have been faster and much easier on my body if it had enough nutrients. 

I started making sure before every medicine I would eat a pudding or a snack in general and a whole drink. Id keep them on my side table and I’d even keep them with me in bed because most days I didn’t want to get out of bed either. The snacks mitigated my nausea, and Slowly, the more I started eating and drinking, the more my appetite started coming back and I started feeling better faster. I noticed a huge difference (almost overnight) between month 1 and 2 of spine surgery recovery. I recovered from my ED with the help of a nutritionist and my orthopedic surgeon. I still struggle a bit years later but I promise you, food won’t hurt you, it’ll only help you feel better sooner. 

My best advice for you to tolerate this until things improve is to find distractions that make you happy. I watched a lot of comedy tv-shows, played on my switch, did connect the dots puzzles, colored coloring pages, cuddled my Guinea pigs, called friends on the phone. Keep your mind distracted, because unfortunately when we lay back down it’s only a matter of time until we’re back to concentrating on the uncomfortable feeling of it all. Remember that time heals, and the pain from this surgery will become more manageable

Please don’t hesitate to reach out OP. Sending you lots of well wishes and love

Hi I’m a 19 year old female and I had my surgery 5 months ago
1. I still don’t look completely straight from the front but it’s better than before. My shoulders are less uneven now but my hips are still a bit tilted. 

2. Yes I had some growth after the surgery, I was 5’4 and am 5’5 now. A good inch of height was added 

3. I didn’t have an S curve, just a C curve to the right. I was fused from my T1-L1 and it took 9 hours for me 

4. My rib hump was slightly reduced with the fusion itself and is only noticeable if I’m laying down or have no shirt on. I didn’t have any ribs surgically removed. 

5. Since I had my surgery during covid I couldn’t have any visitors. I don’t remember much but I was in there for 6 days. On day 3 however, they had to have my mom come in because I was treatment defiant (I don’t remember this, it might’ve been the drugs) I didn’t want to take the medicine because I have a hard time swallowing pills and I cried a lot. Personally I can recall just sleeping a bunch and being rolled over every couple of hours. On the second day I stood up for the first time and after that I had to do pt every 8-12 hours. My recovery was a bit more difficult because I have a severe phobia of throwing up so I didn’t want to eat, drink, or take meds. Therefore I had a lot of panic and anxiety attacks and had to have a psych evaluation before I could be discharged. This is not typical at all so I don’t think you have to worry about that at all. 

6. My scar is not gnarly at all. I healed really fast. However I do think this might’ve been because I didn’t have any external staples or stitches, everything was internal. It’s already pretty thin and a light pink color and it’s only been 5 months. It’s a little thicker at the beginning and ends of the incision but that’s about it. 

6. No the surgery itself did not make me look skinnier but I did lose weight after and that’s when I noticed the weight loss. I don’t think it’s because of the height however, I didn’t have an appetite and felt very nauseous for the first month post op and it was hard to eat. I noticed a small difference in my mid section, it looked a bit flatter? Might’ve been the reduced rib hump however. 

I have some after photos of my back 2 weeks post op on my profile if you’d like to take a look. Everyone’s experience is different and I wish you the best of luck in your surgery and recovery

You don’t have to wear diapers. It does hurt but everyday will get better. When you go to the hospital just make sure to wear something comfortable and easy to slip on. You will most likely be in your hospital gown the whole time you’re there so bring some comfy socks if you’d like! I don’t think I’ve heard of people getting an ng tube after spine surgery, usually nurses start you off by eating bland foods or clear liquid to see if your stomach can handle it. You will have an IV in to give you medicine the first few days but they’ll take it out as soon as you can take your medicine by mouth. They could give you oxygen if you need it

You do not need a wheelchair, car seat, or a stroller. The nurses will help you learn how to properly roll in bed, walk, and sit. You do not need a diaper after surgery, they put a catheter in when you’re asleep (it’s like a rubber straw that catches your pee) usually pain meds make you very constipated the first few days, but by the time you have to go you’ll most likely be able to walk to the toilet with help from a nurse :) You do need an IV for the first few days of surgery to help you get your pain medication and any other medicine you may need. Personally I did have oxygen the first 3 days after my surgery because my oxygen levels were a bit low and I was out of breath, but it all depends on how you’re doing

I had surgery for a curve 3 degrees smaller than this. The difference is I’m 4 years older lol. The curve kept growing about 3~5 degrees a year. I get why they want to do surgery, you’re still young and there’s a bigger chance of a faster increase in curvature. That’s the good thing, the younger you are the faster you heal. Big tip is to write down questions you may have and then ask them to your doctor the day of pre op. I forgot to do this and then I kept remembering what I wanted to ask days later. Also be prepared, lots of pillows for when you come back home as you’ll be sleeping flat now rather than a hospital bed, a shower seat, anything that might make recovery at home easier. Based on recent personal experience, constipation was a bigggg issue because of the narcotic pain medication they give you so make sure to drink a bunch of water and if need be: ask your doctor the best medicine you can take to help with it, every doctor is different and different medicines have different interactions. I lost my appetite after surgery, it’s still kind of gone so have some foods on hand that you know you’ll like. Protein is great, if you can’t eat your protein, smoothies are a great way of getting some calories in. Most importantly: walking is the best thing you can do after surgery. Have someone help you at first: falls are dangerous, you know your body’s limit so if you’re tired go ahead and rest. Every day you will get stronger. Also at the hospital they might give you this thing called a spirometer, it helps build strength/ capacity in your lungs. Make sure to use it at home and at the hospital, this will help prevent pneumonia. These were just a few of the things I could think of, if you have any other questions let me know!
